nodes.summary: Let $1 \le m \le n$ and $1 \le k \le n$, and let $w = (w_1, \dots, w_{m-1})$ be a word with entries in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the set of spots $j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ for which $(j, w_1, \dots, w_{m-1})$ is a partial parking function with $m$ cars and $n$ spots equals $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ if and only if $w$ lies in the set $\mathrm{Sh}_m(k - 1, n - k)$ of $(m, n)$-parking-function shuffles with parameter $k$.
nodes.title: Parking-function shuffles and the first entry

nodes.summary: Let $m \le n$. Every partial parking function $f$ with $m$ cars and $n$ spots is a $t$-metered parking function for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Classical parking functions are metered parking functions

nodes.summary: Let $m \le n$ and $t \ge m - 1$. A map $f : \{0, \dots, m-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a $t$-metered parking function if and only if it is a partial parking function with $m$ cars and $n$ spots.
nodes.title: Metered parking functions with a long meter are classical

nodes.summary: Let $0 < m \le n$ and $f : \{0, \dots, m-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then $f$ is a $1$-metered parking function if and only if, in the lace decomposition of $(f(0), \dots, f(m-1))$, the last spot $n - 1$ occurs in no lace other than as its first entry.
nodes.title: One-metered parking functions and laces

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $f : \{0, \dots, m-1\} \to \{0, 1\}$. Then $f$ is a $1$-metered parking function with $m$ cars and $2$ spots if and only if every lace of the lace decomposition of $(f(0), \dots, f(m-1))$ that contains the value $1$ has length $1$.
nodes.title: One-metered parking functions with two spots

nodes.summary: Let $k > 0$ and $f : \{0, \dots, n+k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\pi_0, \dots, \pi_{n-1}$ be the $(n-1)$-metered outcome of the first $n$ preferences $(f(0), \dots, f(n-1))$ on $n$ spots, where $\pi_c$ is the spot in which car $c$ parks, if it parks. Then $f$ is an $(n-1)$-metered parking function if and only if $(f(0), \dots, f(n-1))$ is a parking function and, for every $i \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, car…
nodes.title: Metered parking functions with meter $n - 1$ and more cars than spots

nodes.summary: Let $2 < m \le n + 1$, $f : \{0, \dots, m-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, $1 \le k \le n$ and $j \in \mathbb{N}$. Write $\mathrm{Sh}_p(q - 1, N - q)$ for the set of $(p, N)$-parking-function shuffles with parameter $q$, words of length $p - 1$ with entries in $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. Suppose that the middle word $w = (f(1), \dots, f(m-2))$ lies in $\mathrm{Sh}_{m-1}(k - 1, n - k)$, and that either $m = n + 1$ and $j = 0$,…
nodes.title: Characterization of $(m-2)$-metered parking functions

nodes.summary: Let $m, n, t \in \mathbb{N}$, number the $n$ spots $0, \dots, n-1$, and let $f : \{0, \dots, m-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ give the preferred spot of each of $m$ cars. In the $t$-metered scheme the cars arrive in the order $0, 1, \dots, m-1$, and car $i$ parks in the least spot $s$ with $f(i) \le s \le n - 1$ that is not occupied by any of the (at most $t$) cars that arrived just before car $i$; it fails to park if…
nodes.title: Metered parking function

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le m \le n$ and $1 \le k \le n$, and write $\mathrm{Sh}_m(k - 1, n - k)$ for the set of $(m, n)$-parking-function shuffles with parameter $k$, words of length $m - 1$ with entries in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then $|\mathrm{Sh}_m(k - 1, n - k)|$ equals $\binom{m-1}{n-k}(n-m+1)\,k^{m-n+k-2}(n-k+1)^{n-k-1}$ if $k > n - m + 1$, equals $m^{m-2}$ if $k = n - m + 1$, and equals $0$ if $k < n - m + 1$. The exponent…
nodes.title: Number of parking-function shuffles

nodes.summary: The word $(2, 6, 1, 0, 6, 1)$ with entries in $\{0, \dots, 7\}$, which is $(3, 7, 2, 1, 7, 2)$ in one-based values, is a $(7, 8)$-parking-function shuffle with parameter $k = 6$, that is, it lies in $\mathrm{Sh}_7(5, 2)$. In one-based values it is a shuffle of the parking function $(3, 2, 1, 2)$ with $4$ cars and $5$ spots and of $(7, 7) = (1, 1) + (6, 6)$.
nodes.title: An example of a parking-function shuffle

nodes.summary: Let $m'$, $n$, $k$ be natural numbers and let $\pi : \{0, \dots, m' - 1\} \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, with one-based letters $w_i = \pi(i) + 1$. Then $\pi$ is a parking-function shuffle with parameters $(m', n, k)$ when all of the following hold: no letter $w_i$ equals $k$; exactly $\max(m' + k - n, 0)$ letters satisfy $w_i < k$; exactly $\max(n - k, 0)$ letters satisfy $w_i > k$; for every $s$ with…
nodes.title: Parking-function shuffles
Examples of lace decompositions

nodes.summary: A lace is a sequence of natural numbers of the form $(p)$ or $(p, p, p+1, \dots, p+\ell-2)$ for some natural number $p$ and some length $\ell \ge 2$. The lace decomposition of a finite sequence $(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ of natural numbers is its partition into blocks of consecutive entries built greedily from left to right: starting with no blocks, each entry $a_i$ in turn is appended to the last block if the result is…
nodes.title: Lace decomposition

nodes.summary: Given a list of blocks (each a list of natural numbers) and a natural number $a$: if the last block is $(p)$ with $a = p$, or the last block has at least two entries and ends with $e$ where $a = e + 1$, then $a$ is appended to the last block; otherwise, including when there is no block, a new block $(a)$ is added at the end.
nodes.title: One step of the lace decomposition

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 2$, $n \ge 2$ and $t \le m - 1$. The number of $t$-metered $(m, n)$-parking functions in which every car parks in its preferred spot is $n(n-1)\cdots(n-t+1) \cdot (n-t)^{m-t}$, where the falling factorial $n(n-1)\cdots(n-t+1)$ has $t$ factors (it equals $1$ for $t = 0$ and $0$ for $t > n$).
nodes.title: Metered parking functions in which every car is lucky

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $t$, $m$, $n$ and a preference function $f : \{0, \dots, m - 1\} \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ (car $i$ prefers spot $f(i)$), the lucky count of $f$ under the $t$-metered parking scheme on $n$ spots is the number of cars $i$ that park in their preferred spot $f(i)$.
nodes.title: Lucky cars in the metered scheme

nodes.summary: Let $t$, $m$, $n$ be natural numbers, let $f : \{0, \dots, m - 1\} \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ be a preference function and let $i < m$ be a car. Under the $t$-metered parking scheme on $n$ spots, if car $i$ parks in spot $s$ then $s \le f(i) + t$, that is, its displacement is at most $t$; and if car $i$ fails to park then $f(i) + t \ge n$.
nodes.title: Displacement bound in the metered scheme

nodes.summary: On the six spots $\{0, \dots, 5\}$, for seven cars with preferences $(2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5)$, the $2$-metered parking scheme parks the cars in spots $(2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 4, 5)$, while in the $1$-metered scheme the first six cars park in spots $(2, 3, 2, 3, 4, 5)$ and the seventh car fails to park.
nodes.title: Metered outcomes of a seven-car example on six spots

nodes.summary: In the $1$-metered parking scheme on two spots $\{0, 1\}$, if three cars arrive with preferences $0$, $0$, $1$, then the first two cars park in spots $0$ and $1$ and the third car fails to park.
nodes.title: A 1-metered example in which the third car fails

nodes.summary: In the $1$-metered parking scheme on two spots $\{0, 1\}$, if three cars arrive all preferring spot $0$, then they park in spots $0$, $1$ and $0$, in that order.
nodes.title: A 1-metered example in which every car parks

nodes.summary: Let $t, n \in \mathbb{N}$, number the $n$ spots $0, \dots, n-1$, and let $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{m-1}$ be a list of preferences in $\mathbb{N}$. Cars arrive in order, and car $i$ parks in the least spot $s$ with $a_i \le s < n$ that is not taken by one of the previous $t$ cars (cars $\max(0, i - t), \dots, i - 1$) that parked; if there is no such spot, car $i$ fails. The outcome is the list whose $i$-th entry is the…
nodes.title: Outcome of the metered parking scheme

nodes.summary: Let $m, n, t$ be natural numbers with $m > n$ and $t \ge n$. Then there are no $t$-metered $(m, n)$-parking functions, that is, $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t) = 0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing of metered parking counts

nodes.title: Binet formula for 1-metered parking functions

nodes.title: 1-metered parking functions with as many cars as spots

nodes.title: Lucas-type recursion for 1-metered parking functions

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the number of $1$-metered $(3, n)$-parking functions is $\mathrm{mpf}_{3,n}(1) = n^3 - 2n$.
nodes.title: 1-metered parking functions with three cars

nodes.summary: The number of $1$-metered $(2, 2)$-parking functions is $\mathrm{mpf}_{2,2}(1) = 3$.
nodes.title: 1-metered parking functions with two cars and two spots

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ be a natural number. The number $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,m-1}(m-2)$ of $(m-2)$-metered $(m, m-1)$-parking functions equals the sum, over all parking functions $f$ of length $m - 1$, of $f(0) + 1$ (the preferred spot of the first car, with spots numbered from $1$), and it also equals
nodes.title: Metered parking functions with one spot fewer than cars

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be natural numbers with $2 < m \le n + 1$. Then the number $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(m-2)$ of $(m-2)$-metered $(m, n)$-parking functions is
nodes.title: Closed form for (m-2)-metered parking functions

nodes.summary: For every natural number $t \ge 1$ and every natural number $n$, the number of $t$-metered $(2, n)$-parking functions is $\mathrm{mpf}_{2,n}(t) = \max(n^2 - 1, 0)$, that is, $n^2 - 1$ for $n \ge 1$ and $0$ for $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Metered parking functions with two cars

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $t$, $m$ and $n$, $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t)$ is the number of $t$-metered $(m, n)$-parking functions, that is, of maps $f$ from the $m$ cars $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ to the $n$ spots $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ under which every car parks in the $t$-metered parking scheme.
nodes.title: Number of metered parking functions

If $(a_1, \dots, a_m)$ is a $t$-metered $(m, n)$-parking function, then for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le n$ and every $j$ with $1 \le j \le m - t$ (truncated subtraction, so there is no such $j$ when $m \le t$),
nodes.title: Window condition for metered parking functions

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le m \le j < k \le n$ and number the spots $1, \dots, n$. The number of $1$-metered $(m, n)$-parking functions whose last car parks in spot $j$ equals the number of those whose last car parks in spot $k$.
nodes.title: Equal last-spot counts for 1-metered parking functions

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le m \le n$ and number the spots $1, \dots, n$. The number of $1$-metered $(m, n)$-parking functions whose last car parks in spot $n$ equals $\mathrm{mpf}_{m-1,n}(1)$, the number of $1$-metered $(m - 1, n)$-parking functions.
nodes.title: 1-metered parking functions whose last car parks in the last spot

nodes.summary: Let $0 < m \le n$ and let $\alpha = (a_1, \dots, a_m)$, with each $a_i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$, be any sequence of preferred spots of $m$ cars on $n$ spots. Under the $1$-metered parking scheme, car $i$ is lucky (it parks in its preferred spot $a_i$) if and only if position $i$ is the first position of one of the laces of the lace decomposition $\mathrm{lace}(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: Lucky cars of 1-metered parking are the lace starts

nodes.title: Parking functions with a given first entry

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $t$, $m$ and $n$, $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t) \ge (n - t)^m$, where $n - t$ is truncated subtraction (equal to $0$ when $t \ge n$).
nodes.title: Lower bound for the number of metered parking functions
Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
